summary: First testing iteration. Backend: 6/7 pytest tests pass; 1 CRITICAL bug — file upload to POST /api/leads returns 422 (Pydantic v2 cannot validate Optional[List[UploadFile]] = File(None)). Frontend: All sections (Navbar, Hero, Services, Before/After, Logistics, Survey, Portfolio with filters, Reviews, Footer) render correctly with proper data-testids. Lead form full-flow works perfectly without files: validation toast for empty submit, POST /api/leads returns 200, new tab opens to wa.me/6282136019744 with correctly prefilled message including Ref ID. No console errors.

critical.issue: Returns 422 'Input should be a valid list' when ANY file is attached. Root cause: `files: Optional[List[UploadFile]] = File(None)` in server.py line 96 is incompatible with Pydantic v2.13 / FastAPI multipart handling — pydantic tries to validate a single UploadFile against List[UploadFile] schema. Reproduced with both 1 and 2 files. Frontend file-upload feature is therefore completely broken end-to-end.

integration_issues.issue: If user attaches any photo/video and submits, backend returns 422 → user sees 'Gagal mengirim' toast. Without files, the flow works perfectly. Caused by backend bug above.

action_items: FIX server.py line 96: change `files: Optional[List[UploadFile]] = File(None)` to `files: List[UploadFile] = File(default=[])` (or use `Annotated[list[UploadFile], File()] = []`). This is the standard FastAPI pattern for optional multi-file uploads and is required for Pydantic v2 compatibility. After fix, retest test_create_lead_with_file_and_static_serve.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `files: Optional[List[UploadFile]] = File(None)` is incompatible with current FastAPI+Pydantic v2 — must be `List[UploadFile] = File(default=[])`.
server.py: Uses deprecated `@app.on_event('shutdown')` — consider migrating to FastAPI lifespan context manager.
server.py uploaded filename sanitization only strips / and \ — does not block traversal via '..' or null bytes. Consider stricter sanitization or use uuid-based stored names.
No file-size limit / content-type validation on uploads; could be exploited for large/malicious files.
CORS allow_origins falls back to '*' with allow_credentials=True which is invalid per spec; either restrict origins or set credentials False.
seed_data_creation: Test leads with TEST_ prefix inserted via pytest (test_create_lead_basic_no_files, test_create_lead_with_file_and_static_serve attempt) and one TEST_PWUser lead from Playwright UI test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers all leads/status endpoints + static upload serving. Only test_create_lead_with_file_and_static_serve fails — will pass once main agent fixes the `files` parameter signature in server.py. Frontend UI fully verified — no need to re-test if backend bug is patched; just re-run pytest.
rca_of_the_issue: Reproduction: `curl -F name=T -F location=X -F camera_count=2 -F building_type=ruko -F ceiling_condition=gypsum -F files=@some.png $BACKEND_URL/api/leads` returns 422 with detail `Input should be a valid list` for body.files. RCA: FastAPI passes UploadFile objects to pydantic for validation; with `Optional[List[UploadFile]] = File(None)` the type is `List[UploadFile] | None` and pydantic v2 receives a single UploadFile (or list of one) but its model schema can't coerce. Fix: declare as `files: List[UploadFile] = File(default=[])`. Mitigation until fixed: users can submit form without attachments — that path works.
